story:
THE TIME JOURNEY BEGINS!

Ding ding... The Time Machine is now activated!
Can you hear it?
From far away in the flow of time, stories from thousands of years ago are still quietly echoing. They aren't found only in history books-they have also been preserved in ancient artifacts.
Today, our travel companion is the Đông Sơn Bronze Drum.
This remarkable drum will take us back to the Văn Lang Kingdom, the earliest traditional Vietnamese state, closely associated with the legendary Hùng Kings.
Are you ready?
Then let's step through the doorway of time together!

Traveling Back to the Văn Lang Period...

We arrive in a vast land along great rivers such as the Red River, Mã River, and Cả River. Long ago, the ancient Vietnamese people had already learned how to grow rice, catch fish, raise livestock, and make tools from bronze. As their lives became more stable, villages and communities grew stronger by working together and protecting the places they called home.
According to Vietnamese historical tradition, the Hùng Kings founded the Kingdom of Văn Lang, regarded as the first state of the Vietnamese people. During this period, bronze casting reached an impressive level of craftsmanship. Skilled artisans created beautiful bronze drums decorated with detailed patterns that reflected both their artistic talent and the daily lives of their communities.
Archaeological research suggests that these bronze drums were used during ceremonies, festivals, and important community gatherings. Their powerful sound may have echoed through rituals praying for favorable weather and abundant harvests, while also bringing people together during significant occasions.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Have you ever imagined that... a drum could tell stories?
The bronze drum in front of us doesn't contain a single written word about the past. Yet somehow, its silence allows every carved pattern to become a special language left behind by the ancient people.
Take a closer look.
At the center of the drum is a shining multi-pointed star, spreading outward in every direction. Around it are rings of detailed designs: birds soaring through the sky, people dancing together, stilt houses beside the rivers, and boats gliding across the water. Together, they create a vivid picture of life long ago.
From these images, archaeologists have learned more about the ancient Vietnamese people. They discovered that these communities farmed, mastered bronze casting, celebrated festivals together, and lived in close-knit societies.
Every small pattern is like a tiny memory, quietly sharing a story from the past.

ARCHAEOLOGY DISCOVERY STATION

Now, slowly rotate the bronze drum and explore every detail!
🔎 Can you find the star at the center of the drum?
🕊️ Can you spot the birds flying around the decorative bands?
🚣 Can you discover the boats, stilt houses, or people carved into the patterns?

Every detail you uncover is another piece of the puzzle, helping us better understand the lives of our ancestors more than two thousand years ago.

SOMETHING TO REMEMBER...

Time has taken many things away.
But it has also carefully preserved others inside ancient artifacts, allowing us to see them and listen to their stories today.
The Đông Sơn Bronze Drum is one of those priceless treasures. Through its surviving patterns, it helps us understand the daily life, creativity, and spiritual world of the people of Văn Lang-people who laid some of the earliest foundations of Vietnam's long history.
And somewhere out there, many more ancient artifacts are still quietly waiting for young explorers like you to discover them...

story:
THE TIME JOURNEY BEGINS!

Ding ding... The Time Machine is now activated!
Can you hear it?
Far back in the flow of history was a time when people worked hard to build their lives while also finding ways to protect their homeland.
Today, our travel companion is the Liên Châu Crossbow, a model inspired by the legendary Cổ Loa Magic Crossbow.
This remarkable crossbow will take us back more than two thousand years to the Âu Lạc Kingdom.
Are you ready?
Then let's step through the doorway of time together!

Traveling Back to the Âu Lạc Period...

We've arrived at Cổ Loa, in present-day Hanoi.
Long ago, this was an important place where people lived, farmed, and built an enormous fortified city.
According to Vietnamese historical tradition, King An Dương Vương chose Cổ Loa as the capital of the Âu Lạc Kingdom. The city was protected by three large earthen walls. Outside the walls, connected moats formed a unique defensive system.
Seen from above, the winding walls resemble the spiral shell of a giant snail. That is how Cổ Loa got its name.
The people of this time grew rice, caught fish, cast bronze, and crafted many tools for everyday life. To defend their city, they also developed increasingly advanced weapons.
At Cổ Loa, archaeologists have discovered thousands of bronze arrowheads, casting molds, and crossbow trigger mechanisms. These findings show that the ancient Vietnamese possessed highly developed metalworking and weapon-making skills.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Did you know...
The Liên Châu Crossbow doesn't tell only a story about battles.
It also tells a story of intelligence, craftsmanship, and the determination of ancient people to protect their homeland.
A crossbow has three main parts: the stock, the bowstring, and the trigger. When the trigger is pulled, the bowstring is released with great force, sending an arrow flying.
In Vietnamese legend, the Liên Châu Crossbow was said to be an extraordinary weapon capable of firing many arrows at once. This magical ability is one of the most memorable parts of the legend of the Cổ Loa Magic Crossbow.
Legends help us imagine the hopes and dreams of people in the past. Meanwhile, real archaeological discoveries-such as bronze arrowheads, casting molds, and crossbow triggers-help archaeologists better understand what life was actually like during the Âu Lạc period.

ARCHAEOLOGY DISCOVERY STATION

Now, slowly rotate the crossbow model and take a closer look!
🏹 Can you point out the stock, the bowstring, and the trigger?
🔎 Can you guess which part releases the bowstring when the trigger is pulled?
🌟 Did you notice? Every small detail on this model is another piece of the puzzle that brings us closer to understanding history.

SOMETHING TO REMEMBER...

Some stories are passed down through legends.
Others are revealed through archaeological discoveries.
When we put these two pieces together, we gain a richer understanding of the Âu Lạc period-a time when the ancient Vietnamese built fortified cities, mastered bronze casting, and worked together to protect their communities.
And somewhere out there, many more ancient artifacts are still quietly waiting for young explorers like you to discover them...

story:
THE TIME JOURNEY BEGINS!

Ding ding... The Time Machine is now activated!
Can you hear it?
Somewhere along a wide, flowing river, the waves are quietly telling an extraordinary story-a story about people who used intelligence, courage, and teamwork to defend their homeland.
Today, our travel companion is the Bạch Đằng Wooden Stake Battlefield Diorama.
This battlefield model will take us back more than one thousand years to a battle that marked the beginning of a new chapter in Vietnam's history.
Are you ready?
Then let's step through the doorway of time together!

Traveling Back to the Ngô Dynasty...

Let's journey back to the Bạch Đằng River in the year 938 CE.
At that time, the Southern Han fleet sailed toward Vietnam with large warships. Ngô Quyền chose this river as the place for the decisive battle.
According to historical records, sharpened wooden stakes were driven deep into the riverbed in areas affected by the tides.
When the tide was high, the stakes remained hidden beneath the water. Ngô Quyền's forces used small boats to lure the enemy fleet farther into the river before retreating.
As the tide fell, the sharpened stakes slowly emerged. The large enemy ships became trapped or were pierced by the stakes, while Ngô Quyền's troops launched their attack from several directions.
The victory at the Battle of Bạch Đằng in 938 opened a new era of independence. In 939, Ngô Quyền proclaimed himself king, established his capital at Cổ Loa, and founded the Ngô Dynasty.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Did you know...
The wooden stakes in this model are much more than sharpened logs placed beneath a river.
They were part of an ingenious military strategy.
Ngô Quyền and his people carefully observed the tides, learning exactly when the water would rise and when it would fall. By understanding nature so well, they turned the Bạch Đằng River into a powerful ally in defending their homeland.
As you look at the pointed tips of the stakes, imagine the determination of the people who prepared them-working together, fighting together, and protecting their country together.

ARCHAEOLOGY DISCOVERY STATION

Now, slowly rotate the model and take a closer look!
🔎 Can you spot the sharpened tips of the wooden stakes?
⛵ What do you think would happen to the large warships when the tide went out? Would they still be able to sail safely?
Every small detail helps us understand one of the most brilliant military strategies in Vietnamese history.

SOMETHING TO REMEMBER...

Sometimes, even something as simple as a wooden stake beneath a river can change the course of history.
When placed in the right place, at the right time, by people working together with wisdom and determination, ordinary things can achieve extraordinary results.
The Bạch Đằng Battlefield Diorama reminds us of the intelligence, courage, and unwavering spirit of the ancient Vietnamese people as they defended their homeland.
From those rows of wooden stakes beneath the river, a new chapter in Vietnam's history began.
And somewhere out there, many more ancient artifacts are still quietly waiting for young explorers like you to discover them...

story:
THE TIME JOURNEY BEGINS!

Ding ding... The Time Machine is now activated!
Can you hear it?
A treasure has been resting quietly beneath the earth for more than a thousand years.
But here's the surprising part-it isn't made of gold or silver. It's not a royal crown or a king's sword.
It's simply... a brick.
Sounds surprising, doesn't it?
Today, our travel companion is the brick inscribed with the words "Đại Việt Quốc Quân Thành Chuyên." This small brick will take us back to the Đinh Dynasty, when Vietnam was beginning a brand-new chapter after many years of division.
Are you ready?
Then let's step through the doorway of time together!

Traveling Back to the Đinh Dynasty...

Our Time Machine stops in the breathtaking mountains of Hoa Lư. Towering limestone cliffs surround the capital like enormous natural walls, providing protection from every side.
At that time, the country had just emerged from years of conflict. After unifying the land by ending the period of the Twelve Warlords, Đinh Bộ Lĩnh became Emperor in 968 CE, established the nation of Đại Cồ Việt, and chose Hoa Lư as its capital.
But building a capital required more than the vision of an emperor-it also depended on the skill and hard work of countless craftsmen.
Imagine this...
There were no excavators, cranes, or modern construction equipment. There was only clay, wooden molds, blazing kilns, and dedicated workers carefully shaping one brick after another.
Once molded and dried, each brick was fired at high temperatures. Before firing, skilled craftsmen carefully carved the inscription "Đại Việt Quốc Quân Thành Chuyên" onto its surface.
One by one, these small bricks were placed together to build city walls, palaces, and important buildings throughout Hoa Lư.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Have you ever imagined that... a brick could tell a story?
At first glance, this brick looks quite simple. It has no elaborate decorations or unusual shape.
But if you look closely, you'll notice the Chinese characters carved into its surface.
Those words are like a message sent to us from more than one thousand years ago.
The inscription "Đại Việt Quốc Quân Thành Chuyên" tells us that this brick was specially produced for building city walls and other important government structures. Thanks to this inscription, archaeologists have learned more about construction techniques, organized production, and urban planning during the Đinh Dynasty.
What seems like an ordinary brick actually tells the remarkable story of a nation taking its first steps after reunification.
Sometimes, the smallest artifacts preserve the greatest stories in history.

ARCHAEOLOGY DISCOVERY STATION

Now, pick up the brick and take a careful look!
🔎 Can you find the carved inscription on its surface?
🧱 Can you see how its neat rectangular shape would make it easy to fit together with many other bricks?
🏯 Imagine thousands of bricks just like this one stacked together. What kind of walls, palaces, or grand buildings do you think they could create?
Every detail you discover helps us better understand the skilled craftsmen who built the ancient capital of Hoa Lư more than one thousand years ago.

SOMETHING TO REMEMBER...

Not every treasure sparkles like gold or silver.
Some treasures rest quietly beneath the earth for centuries, waiting to be discovered.
The "Đại Việt Quốc Quân Thành Chuyên" brick is one of those treasures. It is more than just a building material-it is a witness to the founding of the ancient capital of Hoa Lư and reflects the technical skill, organization, and vision of the Đinh Dynasty during the early years of Vietnam's independent state.
And somewhere beneath the ground, many more ancient artifacts are still quietly waiting for young explorers like you to uncover them on your next journey through time...

story:
THE TIME JOURNEY BEGINS!

Ding ding... The Time Machine is now activated!
Have you ever wondered...
Before paper money, credit cards, or digital payments, what did people use to buy and sell things?
Today, our travel companion is the Thái Bình Hưng Bảo Coin.
At first glance, it looks like nothing more than a small bronze coin with a square hole in the middle. But don't let its simple appearance fool you!
This little coin will take us back to the Early Lê Dynasty, when Vietnam had successfully defended its independence and was beginning to build a peaceful and prosperous future.
Are you ready?
Then let's step through the doorway of time together!

Traveling Back to the Early Lê Dynasty...

Our Time Machine brings us to the ancient capital of Hoa Lư, more than one thousand years ago.
The days of fierce warfare had gradually come to an end, and life was becoming more peaceful. After leading the people of Đại Cồ Việt to victory against the Song Dynasty in 981 CE, Emperor Lê Đại Hành secured the country's independence. Farmers returned to their rice fields, skilled artisans made pottery, wove cloth, forged tools, and marketplaces became busier than ever.
As trade continued to grow, the royal court introduced a new coin called Thái Bình Hưng Bảo, making buying and selling much more convenient.
Now, imagine this...
We've just stepped into a coin mint from over a thousand years ago.
Inside, glowing furnaces melt bronze into liquid metal. Skilled craftsmen carefully pour it into small molds. As the metal cools, round coins with square holes slowly take shape.
Finally, each coin is engraved with the four Chinese characters "Thái Bình Hưng Bảo." One by one, the coins leave the workshop and find their way into busy marketplaces, helping people trade goods throughout Đại Cồ Việt.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Have you noticed what makes this coin so special?
The coin is round, with a square hole in its center. This clever design made it easy to hold, and people could string many coins together with a cord to carry them while traveling or trading.
But perhaps the most interesting feature is the inscription "Thái Bình Hưng Bảo."
These four characters are more than just the coin's name. They show that the coin was officially issued by the royal court for use throughout the kingdom.
Because many of these coins have survived, archaeologists have learned more about trade, daily life, and the growing prosperity of Đại Cồ Việt during the Early Lê Dynasty.
Sometimes, a single small coin can tell the story of an entire era.

ARCHAEOLOGY DISCOVERY STATION

Now, take a close look at the coin!
🔎 Can you find the square hole in the center?
🪙 Can you spot the four Chinese characters engraved on its surface?
🛍️ What kinds of things do you think people might have bought with this coin at the marketplace over a thousand years ago?
Every detail you discover is another clue that helps us better understand the everyday lives of the people of Đại Cồ Việt.

SOMETHING TO REMEMBER...

Some ancient artifacts are no larger than the palm of your hand.
Yet they can carry the story of an entire civilization.
The Thái Bình Hưng Bảo Coin was more than a tool for buying and selling. It became a symbol of the growing economy and the independence of Đại Cồ Việt during the Early Lê Dynasty.
And somewhere out there, many more ancient artifacts are still quietly waiting for young explorers like you to discover them-each with another fascinating story to tell about Vietnam's journey of building and protecting its nation.

story:
THE TIME JOURNEY BEGINS!

Ding ding... The Time Machine is now activated!
Have you ever noticed...
That dragons can look completely different depending on the time and place they were created?
Some dragons appear mighty and powerful. Others look fierce and majestic.
But today, we're going to meet a very special one.
This is the Lý Dynasty Dragon Head-a dragon that doesn't look frightening at all. Instead, it seems to float gently through the clouds.
Have you ever wondered why people long ago imagined a dragon like this?
Then come along as the Lý Dragon takes us back more than 900 years to one of the most brilliant periods in Vietnamese history!
Are you ready?
Let's step through the doorway of time together!

Traveling Back to the Lý Dynasty...

Our Time Machine arrives in the year 1010 CE.
Ahead of us, a fleet of boats glides along the river toward a new land. This is the moment when Emperor Lý Thái Tổ decides to move the capital from Hoa Lư to Đại La.
According to Vietnamese historical tradition, just as the royal boat reached its destination, a golden dragon rose into the sky. Seeing this as a good omen, the emperor renamed the capital Thăng Long, meaning "Ascending Dragon."
From that moment on, Thăng Long became the heart of the kingdom, growing larger and more prosperous each year.
As the kingdom flourished, so did its architecture and art. These dragon carvings were created not only as decoration but also as symbols of peace, prosperity, and the hope that the nation would continue to rise and thrive.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Have you noticed anything special about this dragon?
Take a closer look!
Its head is quite small, and its mouth is slightly open, almost as if it is smiling. Its long whiskers curve gently backward, while its body flows gracefully like a dragon dancing among the clouds.
According to researchers, dragons from the Lý Dynasty have a unique style that is quite different from dragons created during later periods. Instead of expressing strength through a fierce appearance, they reflect elegance, harmony, and a deep wish for a peaceful and prosperous world.
Every carefully carved line in the stone is like a message left behind nearly one thousand years ago.

ARCHAEOLOGY DISCOVERY STATION

Now, take a close look at the dragon head!
🐉 Can you spot its small head and gently open mouth?
☁️ Can you see the graceful curves that make it look as though it is floating through the clouds?
🏯 Where do you think this dragon head might have been placed on a palace or temple in the ancient capital of Thăng Long?
Every detail you discover helps us appreciate the remarkable skill of the artisans and the beauty of Vietnamese art during the Lý Dynasty.

SOMETHING TO REMEMBER...

Some dragons live only in legends.
Others continue to live through the works of art left behind by generations of skilled craftsmen.
The Lý Dynasty Dragon Head is one of the greatest symbols of Vietnamese art. More than an architectural decoration, it reflects the remarkable achievements of the Lý Dynasty in culture, architecture, and craftsmanship, as well as the enduring dream of building a peaceful and prosperous nation.
And somewhere out there, many more ancient artifacts are still quietly waiting for young explorers like you to discover them...

story:
THE TIME JOURNEY BEGINS!

Ding ding... The Time Machine is now activated!
Can you hear it?
From deep within history come the sounds of horses galloping outside the walls of Thăng Long, soldiers training along the riverbanks, and urgent meetings in the royal court where leaders gathered to discuss the future of the nation.
Today, our travel companion is a Trần Dynasty Royal Seal.
This small seal will take us back to a remarkable period in Vietnamese history-an era when courage, unity, and love for the homeland shaped one of the brightest chapters in the story of Đại Việt.
Are you ready?
Then let's step through the doorway of time together!

Traveling Back to the Trần Dynasty...

We have arrived in Thăng Long during the 13th century.
After the Lý Dynasty came to an end, the Trần Dynasty was established in 1225, beginning nearly 175 years of remarkable history. During this time, Đại Việt flourished in government, culture, and education. At the same time, it faced enormous challenges as it defended the kingdom against invasions by the Mongol Empire and the Yuan Dynasty.
Most famously, Đại Việt successfully defeated the Mongol-Yuan invasions three times, demonstrating the extraordinary courage, unity, and determination of its people.
In 1288, at the Bạch Đằng River, the army led by Trần Hưng Đạo achieved a decisive victory.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Did you know?
A seal may be small, but it carries a great deal of responsibility.
Long ago, whenever the royal court issued an important decree, an official seal was pressed onto the document. That seal told everyone that these were not simply words-they were official orders that carried responsibility.
As we look at this seal today, it invites us to think about three important values:
Authority - to maintain order and govern wisely.
Responsibility - because every decision can affect many people's lives.
Trust - because every seal was a promise that the order should be carried out faithfully.

ARCHAEOLOGY DISCOVERY STATION

Now, hold the seal carefully and take a closer look!
🔎 Can you find the handle at the top of the seal?
📜 Imagine this seal being stamped onto an imperial decree. What kind of message do you think it might contain?

👑 What qualities do you think someone trusted to use this seal should have?

SOMETHING TO REMEMBER...

Some ancient artifacts tell their stories without words.
They rest quietly through the centuries, waiting for someone to look closely enough to discover the history they hold.
The Trần Dynasty Royal Seal reminds us of an era when love for the homeland was shown through meaningful actions-governing wisely, organizing the nation, preparing its defenses, and working together to protect every part of the country.
And somewhere out there, many more ancient artifacts are still quietly waiting for young explorers like you to discover them...

story:
THE TIME JOURNEY BEGINS!

Ding ding... The Time Machine is now activated!
Can you hear it?
Far back in time, across the wide plains of Thanh Hóa, echoes the sound of stone striking stone, people calling to one another as they move enormous blocks of rock.
Today, our travel companion is the Hồ Citadel.
Unlike a small artifact displayed inside a museum case, the Hồ Citadel is a giant artifact-one that has stood proudly beneath the open sky for more than six hundred years.
Are you ready?
Then let's step through the doorway of time together!

Traveling Back to the Hồ Dynasty...

We have arrived in the late 14th century.
At that time, Đại Việt was facing many challenges. The Trần Dynasty was gradually weakening, and the threat of invasion from the north continued to grow.
In response, Hồ Quý Ly decided to build a new capital at An Tôn. During the first three months of 1397, an extraordinary stone citadel began to rise. Massive stone blocks-some weighing tens of tons-were quarried, transported, carefully shaped, and assembled into towering defensive walls.
In 1400, Hồ Quý Ly established the Hồ Dynasty, renamed the country Đại Ngu, and made Tây Đô the capital.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Did you know?
From a distance, the Hồ Citadel looks like an enormous stone fortress.
But when you look more closely, each stone becomes a reminder of the intelligence, determination, and teamwork of the people who built it.
Some of the stones measure several meters in length and weigh between 10 and more than 20 tons. Yet centuries ago, builders managed to lift, transport, and fit them together with astonishing precision.
The Hồ Citadel tells us much more than the story of a royal capital. It tells the story of cooperation, creativity, and the determination of generations who worked together to build their nation.

ARCHAEOLOGY DISCOVERY STATION

Now, take a careful look at the Hồ Citadel!
🪨 Can you spot the enormous stone blocks that form the walls?
🏰 How do you think people long ago lifted and moved stones that weighed so many tons?
🚪 Can you see the beautiful arched gateways? Why do you think arches make a building stronger?
🌿 Imagine the moats, bamboo, mountains, and rivers surrounding the citadel.

SOMETHING TO REMEMBER...

Some ancient artifacts are small enough to fit in the palm of your hand.
Others are so enormous that you must step back to admire their full beauty.

story:
THE TIME JOURNEY BEGINS!

Ding ding... The Time Machine is now activated!
Can you hear it?
In the distance, ceremonial drums echo through the ancient capital of Thăng Long. Officials dressed in elegant court robes cross the Dragon Courtyard and walk toward a magnificent royal hall.
Along the stone staircase, a dragon stretches gracefully from step to step.
It doesn't soar through the clouds.
It doesn't swim beneath the water.
Instead, it quietly watches over the pathway leading to the most important place in the entire royal court.
Today, our travel companion is the Stone Dragon of the Kính Thiên Palace Stairway.
Are you ready?
Then let's step through the doorway of time together!

Traveling Back to the Early Lê Dynasty...

We have arrived in Thăng Long during the 15th century.
After years under Ming rule, the Lam Sơn Uprising successfully restored Vietnam's independence. In 1428 CE, Emperor Lê Thái Tổ ascended the throne, founded the Early Lê Dynasty, and established Kính Thiên Palace within the Imperial Citadel.
Kính Thiên Palace was an extraordinary place.
Here, the emperor held court, discussed matters of state, and presided over important ceremonies. Officials from across the kingdom climbed the stone staircase with respect and solemnity before entering the palace.
Every step brought them closer to the royal hall.
But those steps also served as a reminder that inside were decisions that would shape the lives of the people, the defense of the kingdom, and the future of Đại Việt.
That is why magnificent stone dragons were carved along both sides of the staircase-the most powerful symbol of imperial authority.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Have you ever wondered why this dragon lies beside the staircase?
Long ago, the dragon was closely associated with the emperor.
It symbolized authority, strength, and the hope for a prosperous kingdom. By placing stone dragons along the entrance to Kính Thiên Palace, the royal court created a space of dignity and respect, reminding everyone that they were approaching the very heart of the kingdom.
Now, take a closer look.
The dragon raises its head proudly, gazing forward.
Its large round eyes, long horns, and graceful body flow naturally along the staircase. The ridges on its back resemble swirling clouds and dancing flames.
One detail is especially important:
The dragon has five sharp claws.
In the royal art of the Early Lê Dynasty, dragons with five claws were closely associated with the emperor. This tells us that the staircase led to one of the most important places in the royal capital.
The Stone Dragon of Kính Thiên Palace reminds us of three enduring values:
Authority - because the dragon represents the emperor and the royal court.
Respect - because everyone who climbed these steps was expected to behave with dignity.
Masterful craftsmanship - because skilled artisans transformed solid green stone into a dragon that seems both graceful and alive.

ARCHAEOLOGY DISCOVERY STATION

Now, take a careful look at the dragon!
🐉 Can you see its head held high?
👀 What do you notice about its eyes, horns, and mouth?
🪨 Can you see how its body curves naturally along the stone steps?
🖐️ Can you count how many claws the dragon has?
☁️ Along its back, can you spot the ridges that resemble clouds or dancing flames?
Every carved detail is a message from the past.
If you observe closely, you'll discover how much imagination, skill, and pride the ancient craftsmen poured into every line they carved.

SOMETHING TO REMEMBER...

Long ago, Kính Thiên Palace was one of the grandest buildings in the royal capital.
Although much of the palace has disappeared over time, the stone dragons still remain on the staircase, quietly watching over Thăng Long after hundreds of years.
The Stone Dragon of Kính Thiên Palace tells more than the story of a king or a palace.
It reminds us of an era when the Vietnamese people worked together to build their country, protect its independence, and create beautiful works of architecture that could endure through the centuries.
Whenever we look at this stone dragon, we can remember:
True strength is found not only in authority, but also in the responsibility to protect, preserve, and build a better nation.
And perhaps, beyond this stone dragon, many more ancient artifacts are still waiting for young explorers like you to discover as you continue your journey through Vietnam's history.

Together, we journey back to Đại Việt in the 16th century.
In 1527 CE, Mạc Đăng Dung founded the Mạc Dynasty. Although this was a period of political change, everyday life continued. Farmers worked in the rice fields, merchants traded in busy markets, weavers made cloth, and potters shaped clay into beautiful objects.
Inside glowing pottery kilns, skilled artisans carefully kneaded soft clay before shaping it into bowls, plates, lampstands, and elegant incense burners.
When a stick of incense was lit, its gentle smoke floated slowly through the air, carrying people's hopes for peace and prosperity.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Now, take a closer look!
The burner has a wide opening, a rounded body, and sturdy little feet supporting it from below.
Its surface is decorated with raised patterns that wrap around the body like an elegant robe.
The rich brown glaze, blended with soft gray-blue tones, gives the vessel a warm and timeless beauty.
But this incense burner is more than simply a vessel for burning incense.
It also tells the story of the patient hands of the potters who created it.
From an ordinary lump of clay, through skilled craftsmanship and the intense heat of the kiln, a beautiful ceremonial object came to life.

Sometimes, it lives within the layers of glaze that have aged over centuries, in the carved patterns on ancient pottery, and in the gentle trails of incense that once drifted through old temples.
The Mạc Dynasty Ceramic Incense Burner reminds us that the Vietnamese people were not only master potters, but also artisans who filled their creations with heartfelt wishes for peace, prosperity, and a good life.

Traveling Back to the Later Lê Restoration...

Together, we journey back more than three hundred years into the history of Đại Việt.
By this time, the Lê Dynasty had been restored. In Đàng Ngoài, the Lê emperor remained the symbolic ruler while the Trịnh Lords managed most affairs. Farther south, the Nguyễn Lords governed Đàng Trong.
During this period, the country experienced many years of conflict. Fortresses along rivers, coastal defenses, and important waterways became essential to protecting the land.
One of the most impressive weapons was the royal cannon. These cannons were placed on fortress walls, along riverbanks, and aboard warships.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT

Now, take a closer look!
The royal cannon has a long, thick, and heavy body, much like a giant metal tube.
At the front is the muzzle. Inside runs the long barrel. At the back is the breech, which strengthens and supports the cannon during firing.
To use the cannon, soldiers carefully loaded gunpowder and a cannonball into the barrel. When ignited, the powerful explosion launched the cannonball over a great distance.
Making a royal cannon required extraordinary skill. Craftsmen had to melt large amounts of metal, cast the cannon into a strong shape, and ensure the barrel was smooth and even.

🔎 Can you find the muzzle at the front of the cannon?

This royal cannon is more than an ancient weapon. It is a reminder of the knowledge, craftsmanship, and determination of those who came before us.

In 1558 CE, Nguyễn Hoàng was appointed governor of Thuận Hóa. From this coastal region, the Nguyễn Lords gradually established Đàng Trong, expanding their territory farther south and building a society closely connected to the sea.
For the people of Đàng Trong, the sea was much more than waves and wind. It was a pathway for ships to travel, for merchants to trade, and for ports such as Hội An to grow into bustling centers of commerce.
The Nguyễn Lords placed great importance on building a strong navy. Their fleets patrolled the coastline and protected the lives of people living along the coast.

This was the time when the Tây Sơn movement rose to power. People from many places joined together to build a strong army and protect their country.
Among those soldiers was a very special force-the war elephants.
In the spring of 1789, Emperor Quang Trung led the Tây Sơn army north in a lightning-fast campaign against the Qing army. During the famous Battle of Ngọc Hồi-Đống Đa, the Tây Sơn forces won a remarkable victory.
During the battle, the war elephants charged at the front lines, helping to break the enemy's formations and clearing the way for the Tây Sơn soldiers to advance.

story:
THE TIME TRAVEL BEGINS!

Ding ding... The Time Machine has been activated!
Can you see the golden seal shining brightly?
Long ago, this very seal rested inside the Imperial City of Huế, where it witnessed many important moments in the history of the Nguyễn Dynasty.
Today, our travel companion is the Golden Seal "Hoàng Đế Chi Bảo."
This extraordinary seal will take us back to the reign of Emperor Minh Mạng, where we'll explore life inside the royal palace and discover one of the most powerful symbols of the Vietnamese emperors.
Are you ready?
Then let's step through the Door of Time together!

BACK TO THE NGUYỄN DYNASTY...

Our journey brings us to Đại Việt in the early 19th century.
In 1802, the Nguyễn Dynasty was established, and Huế became the nation's capital. It was the last imperial dynasty in Vietnamese history.
Inside the Imperial City, important work took place every day. The emperor issued royal decrees, met with court officials, held grand ceremonies, and exchanged diplomatic letters with other countries.
Whenever an important document was completed, it was stamped with the Golden Seal "Hoàng Đế Chi Bảo."
That royal seal was the emperor's highest mark of approval.

UNLOCKING THE ARTIFACT!

Take a close look at the seal!
Its body is square, made of gold, and feels strong and solid.
On top sits a powerful dragon, gracefully curling its body. In traditional Vietnamese culture, the dragon symbolizes the emperor, strength, and prosperity.
Turn the seal over, and you'll find four Chinese characters engraved on its base: "Hoàng Đế Chi Bảo," meaning "The Emperor's Treasure."
This seal is much more than a precious object made of gold.
It is a symbol of royal authority, dignity, and the extraordinary craftsmanship of Nguyễn Dynasty artisans.
In 1945, this very seal also witnessed a historic moment when Emperor Bảo Đại handed it over to the Revolutionary Government, marking the end of Vietnam's imperial monarchy.

ARCHAEOLOGY DISCOVERY STATION!

Now, take a careful look at the golden seal!
🐉 Can you spot the dragon resting on top of the seal?
🔍 Can you find the four engraved Chinese characters on the bottom?
✨ Look closely at its square shape and the finely carved details. How carefully do you think the craftsmen had to work to create such a beautiful treasure from solid gold?
Every detail helps us discover more about the art of the royal court and life inside the Imperial City of Huế more than two hundred years ago.

ONE THING TO REMEMBER...

The past doesn't live only in history books.
Sometimes, it is preserved inside a small golden seal that has witnessed some of the most important moments in a nation's history.
The Golden Seal "Hoàng Đế Chi Bảo" reminds us that an artifact is valuable not only because it is made from precious materials, but also because of the stories it carries and the history it has lived through.
And who knows... Somewhere out there, more ancient treasures may still be waiting for you to discover them.
